subject: R²  in mediating variable increases after adding another Dependent Variable?

messages.author: 71eccd0b71a76ddc
messages.subject: R²  in mediating variable increases after adding another Dependent Variable?
parts:
Hi all

I am doing a study for which I tested a model like this:

Model1: Var1 --> var2--> var3 --> var4. All variables are latent variables and have several indicators.

Now, the R² of var3 is +-40% in this case. However, something strange happens when I test the model:

Model2: Var1 --> var2 --> var3.

In this case, although the variables BEFORE var3 remain exactly the same, the R² of var3 becomes much smaller (+-28%).

Does anyone have a possible explanation for this? I've already checked whether this is due to missings in var4 but this is not the case.

You can find the code of both models attached

Thanks in advance

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: R² in mediating variable increases after adding another Dependent Variable?
parts:
It may be that the larger model is misspecified.  If there is a missing path (say, from #1 to #4 or from #2 to #4), then the path from #2 to #4 may be biased to compensate, producing a lower R2 for #3 when #4 is present.  If you add direct paths from #1 and #2 to #4, I bet you will see the decline in #3’s R2 disappear.

--Ed Rigdon

parts:
Thanks for your reply.

I did what you suggested but the R² still remains much higher in the larger model. What I did find out, however, is that when I consider the variables to be manifest in model 1, the R² in var3 is much alike as in model 2 (even though there the variables are considered latent). Off course it is not right to consider them manifest but it seems that the differences in R² are due to the indicators. However, I can not figure out what the difference is between both models in this respect.
